change.purpose: Operator request 2026-10-05: 'Analysera loggfilen från långkörande Greenfield arbete i flera Chrome fönster. Sök om du hittar abnormala händelser, onödiga automatiska rotationer osv. Analysera koden mycket djupt och leverera ny version om fel hittas.'
change.analysis: Diagnostics export 2026-10-05 (v1.8.12, 4 windows, Max parallella 2 with one reserved window, 532 dispatches 09-30 05:00 to 10-05 06:01 UTC; analysed in the scratchpad, not packaged). 30 dispatches never got a completed answer (22 FULL, 8 COMPACT; a 31st was in flight at export). Each held its window and its capacity slot for the whole stale ladder (next dispatch 123-127 min later in the reserved window): 1918 of 5810 minutes (33 %) of the shared slot and 1337 minutes (23 %) of the reserved window, outside budget stops; on 10-01 17:16-19:16 both slots were held by dead turns and all four windows stood still. Four fleet-wide stops match local budget gates (24 h token budget ~2.6 M, 7-day message cap 400) by their 24 h roll-off and policy-update timing; inferred, the policy at the time is not in the export. 76 % of dispatches were FULL fresh-chat prompts (queue design, quantum 1, AI yields). Why answers did not come, the 54-minute same-GFW restart and 5 same-GFW fresh-chat restarts could not be determined: the audit log is volatile by default and the safety events cover about 15 hours.
defects: A turn that showed neither a generation nor an answer after the ladder's 30-minute reload kept its capacity slot until the 120-minute switch; the one-minute recovery scan re-adopted every WAITING turn (reproduced: tests/v1813-stale-turn-slot.test.mjs, 1/9 on v1.8.12)

Diagnostics could not explain automatic stops and rotations: no durable record of stale-ladder steps, rotations, queue switches or safety holds; SAFETY_POLICY_UPDATED carried no values; restart 'restored' rows had no time of their own and showed a days-old restore under the latest scan time
change.implementation: lib/waiting-refresh.mjs staleTurnCapacityDecision (pure). background.js: maybeReleaseStaleTurnCapacity (in maybeEscalateWaitingRefresh's wait path; writes waitingRefresh.capacityReleased before releaseSchedulerTurn), maybeReadoptStaleTurnCapacity (stop button or streaming seen again: adoptSchedulerTurnForObservedEffect, not released again before the next reload stage), potentialActiveTurnDescriptor skips a released turn. lib/incident-log.mjs (eic.gf.incident-log.v1, 400-row ring, ids/codes/numbers/flags only) with rows from the stale ladder (with page evidence), slot hand-back/readopt, armSessionRotation, queue park and activation, safety holds that start or change (pacing excluded), provider content block, tab recovery, restart restore and policy update. lib/startup-diagnostics.mjs exports the incident log, an incident index, the capacity scheduler and the prompt gate. lib/usage-governor.mjs: policy update event lists changed values. Worker card note in lib/operations-view.mjs staleTurnSlotNote and sidepanel.js/css.
change.unchanged: The stale ladder (F5 30, Ctrl-F5 60/90, switch or rotation 120), exact-once dispatch (nothing is resent), answer capture, the queue design (fresh chat per activation), the reserved slot, prompt pacing and every safety budget and its accounting (output reserve) are unchanged.

knownRemainingRisks: After a reload ChatGPT's client polls /conversation/{id}/stream_status and refetches when the answer is complete (read in ChatGPT's public JS 2026-09-26). If no stop button or streaming is shown meanwhile, a still-running answer is counted as dead and its slot is handed back: at most one extra concurrent generation per such turn; the answer is still captured. Not measured live
A page that keeps the composer busy without a stop button keeps the slot (conservative)
The incident log keeps 400 rows; a very busy fleet may roll over in about 2-4 days (droppedRows counts the loss)
Everything listed for 1.8.12 (reservation follows the worker binding, pacing per window) still applies
